title: Cluster 01 DRILL: The Greenhouse Mechanism and Carbon Footprints
subtitle: H2 Biology 9477 · Book 8, Extension Topic B · 9 questions · 89 marks · 31 parts · one mark per minute, so about an hour and a half · every question is an actual exam paper question except one tagged part
intro_html:
Answers sit directly under each part, hidden. Click Show answer only after you have said your full reasoning aloud for that part. Check (a) before you start (b), that is the point of the layout.

Rate your confidence before every reveal. A dashed line sits above each answer block. Say high, medium or guessed out loud before you click. A right answer said hesitantly stays ACTIVE; a right answer said confidently moves on.

Every question below is a real exam paper question, with one exception that says so. The stem is the paper's own wording. Where a stem has been edited it is only so that it stands without the parts of the original that came before it, and the edit is written out in the Sources block at the foot of that question. Question 1(f) is the single constructed part in this drill, written because no question in the 517-record Book 8 the papers asks a candidate to rank energy sources from a supplied table, and it is tagged CONSTRUCTED in its own mark scheme and Sources block.

Every real Book 8 question that could be found is in this set. Book 8's bank and its overflow file is empty, so every real Book 8 question that could be found is already in it, and roughly. This set is therefore built specimen-first: Questions 1, 2 and 3 are the whole of the 9477 specimen's Book 8 content that belongs to this cluster, at their real mark allocations, with the prelim questions arranged around them.

Carbon footprints lead this drill. LOs (c), (d) and (g) carried about two thirds of the specimen's Book 8 marks. Nine parts here are LO (d) and three more are sequestration under LO (c). Drilling this Book off prelim papers alone points at exactly the wrong outcomes.

Six real figures, five questions figure-led. Book 8 is 52.6% figure-led, the highest of any Book, and 49.7% data interpretation. Every figure is the real image from the paper the question came from. What has been cut is the read-off: no part asks you to state a value at a year. The data is stimulus for an explain, a suggest, a calculation or a judgement.

Two MCQs, both real, both audited. The paper awards one mark for the letter. The drill then asks you to explain the answer, which is where every option gets justified.

Cumulative over Books 1, 3, 5 and 7. Q1(a) is allopatric speciation from Book 7 and nothing else, and it is 5 of the real 13 marks. Q2(a) is Book 1 biomolecules. Q4 needs the Calvin cycle and the link reaction and Krebs cycle said cold from Book 5. Q5(b) needs enzyme kinetics from Book 1 driving oxidative decarboxylation. A Book 1, 5 or 7 gap surfacing here is worth more than a clean Book 8 answer, so say it out loud when it happens.

What the marks reward. Say absorb and re-emit, never retain or hold, and expect a scheme to make that sentence compulsory even in a question that looks like it is only about human activities. Never name a human activity without the gas or the mechanism that follows it. Read whether the stem said direct or indirect, because the schemes reject the wrong half by name. Take every GWP and every footprint figure off the table you are given, never out of memory. On a calculation write heading, formula, working, unit, stated significant figures, because a scheme in this set caps you at 1 mark with no headings at all. On a comment or discuss part take one stance and bound it, because a both-sides answer is penalised by name.

One primary concept each, checked for duplicated required answers as well as duplicated labels. Q1 the whole Book 8 specimen anchor, speciation then the direct-indirect split then three LO (d) mechanisms then a ranking judgement · Q2 sequestration as named biomolecules, then arithmetic, then a judgement against your own number · Q3 CO2e computed across five gases, potency held apart from total contribution · Q4 the carbon cycle end to end and why a large sink still leaves a net rise · Q5 sink and source defined by net direction, and what flips one into the other · Q6 the properties that separate CO2 from methane, and a rate-of-change axis · Q7 the land and food side of the footprint · Q8 proxies, and describing a record with quoted data · Q9 the discuss archetype at full length.

The three deliberately shared marking points, declared. First, greenhouse gases absorb longwave or infrared radiation and re-emit it, trapping heat in the atmosphere, which a prelim scheme in this Book makes a compulsory point even inside a question about human activities; it is required in Q4, Q5(c) and Q6(c) and that repetition is the point. Second, deforestation removes a carbon sink, which Q1(b) needs as its whole answer and Q7(a) needs as one of two routes from meat production to CO2; the two are not interchangeable, because Q1(b) is marked on the word indirect and Q7(a) is marked on land conversion. Third, crop plants absorb CO2 as they grow, offsetting what is released on combustion, which Q1(d) needs alone and Q9 needs as one of twelve possible marks. Every other required answer in the set is unique.

Nothing from Book 9, and nothing from chapter 8.1 beyond the greenhouse mechanism. Roughly 12% of chapter 8.1 is examinable, 26 pages carrying about 3. Albedo, biomes, El Nino, orbital cycles and volcanic aerosols are out; LO (a) is explicit that the outcome is anthropogenic. Nitrous oxide appears only where a paper printed it, because LO (a) says limited to CO2 and methane. Mangroves, coral, feedback loops and the effects on organisms are Cluster 2; food supply, biodiversity and dengue are Cluster 3.
